interest: This file provides valuable insight into the expansion of Japanese naval diplomacy in Southeast Asia during the mid-to-late 1930s, specifically targeting Siam (Thailand) as Tokyo sought closer geopolitical ties in the region prior to World War II. The repeated port calls by Imperial Japanese Navy training squadrons and cruisers—including the Kuma, Asama, Yakumo, and Iwate—illustrate Japan's strategic projection of naval presence and goodwill missions along the Menam River and at Bangkok. Additionally, the document is useful for understanding State Department record-keeping and decimal filing practices, demonstrating how cross-reference docket sheets (Form DS-46) tracked bilateral naval and aviation interactions under Japan's classification (894.3392) while routing the detailed substantive despatches into Siamese internal political files (892.00 P.R.).
keywords: Visits of Japanese Vessels to Siam
overview: This file (894.3392) consists of a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) documenting official records on visits of Japanese naval vessels to Siam (Thailand) between 1934 and 1938. The docket sheet lists four communications from the U.S. Legation in Bangkok, including despatches authored by Chargé d'Affaires Walter C. Baker and Minister Edwin L. Neville, reporting on the port calls and movements of Imperial Japanese Navy warships. Specifically, it indexes reports on the arrival of the cruiser Kuma at Bangkok in February 1934, the visit of the Japanese Training Squadron comprising the cruisers Asama and Yakumo under Rear Admiral Kamisaburo Nakamura in April 1935, and visits by the training ships Iwate and Yakumo in May and June 1938. The underlying despatches were cross-referenced and primarily filed under Siam's political reporting decimal classification (892.00 P.R.), leaving this docket sheet as the consolidated index under the Japanese naval visits classification.
